find:
GRANT UPDATE (state, attempt_count, next_attempt_at, reserved_at, last_attempt_at, completed_at,
  safe_reason_code, updated_at) ON control_owner_push_attempt_heads TO control_room_private_web;
replace: -- MUTATED: the dispatcher's update grant is removed
why: the dispatcher settles every outcome through that column-scoped UPDATE, so without it no item can ever be recorded as delivered and every send fails 42501
a failed send must be re-sendable; without the upgrade clause the retry is read as an existing row, a dead endpoint is reported as delivered, and the phone is never rung

find: WHERE tenant_id=$1 AND action_inbox_id=ANY($3::text[]) AND state='pending'
why: the reserve is the compare-and-set that makes a claim exclusive; without the state test two racing dispatchers both reserve the same item and both send

find: WHERE h.tenant_id=$1 AND h.state='pending' AND h.next_attempt_at<=$2
replace: WHERE h.tenant_id=$1 AND h.state IN ('pending','reserved') AND h.next_attempt_at<=$2
why: only 'pending' is claimable: a 'reserved' row is a send in flight RIGHT NOW, and re-claiming it is a second push for one stall

find: WHERE h.tenant_id=$1 AND h.state='reserved' AND h.reserved_at<=$2
replace: WHERE h.tenant_id=$1 AND h.state='reserved' AND h.reserved_at<=$2 AND false
why: a dispatcher killed between the reservation and the settle leaves a row no tick can ever pick up, so that stall is never pushed for at all

find: const terminal = disposition === "delivered" || disposition === "failed" || spent >= OWNER_PUSH_ATTEMPT_LIMIT_V1;
why: the attempt bound must stop retrying for good, so a permanently dead endpoint cannot send for ever

find:
if (!sendFailure) {
      // No subscription, or a channel that reported success while delivering
replace:
if (false) {
      // No subscription, or a channel that reported success while delivering
why: no-subscription is distinguished from send-failure by the failure report, never by the counters alone
a delivered head must be terminal: without this a caller can rewind it to pending and re-alert the owner for a stall they already answered
the attempt count may never be rewound, so a delivered item cannot be made to look like it was never tried

find: attempt_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (attempt_count BETWEEN 0 AND 8),
replace: attempt_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (attempt_count >= 0),
why: the bound is also enforced by the column, independently of the guard, so a path the guard misses still cannot retry for ever
the stored deep link is a local product path only, so a push can never be an open redirect even if the row were written by a compromised caller
the primary key is the idempotence guarantee: one stall owns exactly one head for its whole life
a push failure is reported as a bare reason code; a raw message would carry the push endpoint URL and the quoted task text into the host log
a down push service at host startup must not fail the host's startup path; the items are still in the inbox and the next tick picks them up
a 404/410 means the browser subscription is gone and has already been removed, so the item must stop for good rather than spend the bounded attempts reaching nothing
